title: Malformed-daily-bar hygiene round 2: non-blocking review follow-up
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #72 (api-stocks-analysis-nullable-indicators-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges/is fixed. This is separate from -- and does not duplicate -- the blocking finding on that same review (a real stop_hit-suppression regression, sent back via `review.verdict: needs_work`), which the task-worker must fix before this follow-up applies.

checklist.step: `TestGetRisk::test_malformed_bar_earlier_in_history_does_not_perturb_stop_or_flags` (backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_risk.py) places its injected malformed (all-NaN) row at the very front (oldest position) of the daily history. Verified by reverting the router's `drop_malformed_daily_bars` call locally: this test still passes even without the fix, because pandas' `Series.ewm(adjust=False).mean()` treats a leading NaN as 'not yet started' and doesn't propagate it into later values, and the swing-low `.min()`/volatility `.mean()` aggregations `protective_stop` uses are `skipna=True` by default -- so a malformed bar at the very oldest position happens to be a structural no-op whether or not it's dropped. (Contrast: a malformed bar in the *middle* of the window does perturb subsequent EMA(13) values with vs. without dropping it -- verified via a standalone `Series.ewm` repro with a mid-series NaN producing different downstream values than the same series with that row removed.) This means the test provides no actual regression protection for the 'malformed bar elsewhere in history' scenario its own docstring describes, even though the production fix (`drop_malformed_daily_bars`, which drops a NaN row unconditionally regardless of position) is still correct for that case. Strengthen the test by placing the malformed row inside the `_SWING_LOW_WINDOW_DAYS`/EMA(13) window instead of at the very start, so it actually fails without the fix the way `test_malformed_bar_that_drops_history_below_minimum_excludes_position` already does.

decisions.decision: Moved the injected malformed row in `test_malformed_bar_earlier_in_history_does_not_perturb_stop_or_flags` from the very front of `clean_daily` (index 0) to after its 2nd row (index 2, via `pd.concat([clean_daily.iloc[:2], malformed_row, clean_daily.iloc[2:]], ...)`), rather than choosing some other in-window position or restructuring the fixture more heavily.
decisions.rationale: Reproduced the task's own claim first, by hand: with the malformed row at the front, `Series.ewm(span=13, adjust=False).mean()` on `[nan, 100.0, 102.0, ...]` produces exactly the same trailing values as `ewm(...)` on `[100.0, 102.0, ...]` alone (pandas treats a leading NaN as 'not yet started', not as a value to propagate) -- confirmed via a standalone repro before touching the test. Inserting after index 2 keeps the fixture's overall shape and every downstream assertion (`_QUIET_STOP`, `expected_risk_pct`, the two flags) completely unchanged, because `drop_malformed_daily_bars` removes the injected row unconditionally regardless of position -- once dropped, the frame is byte-for-byte `clean_daily` again (verified via `DataFrame.equals`), so the fix path's expected values didn't need updating, only the no-fix path's behavior needed to genuinely diverge. Hand-computed (and printed) `protective_stop` on the *undropped* 7-row frame at this insertion point: 98.4624584717608, vs. the reference 98.46530612244898 -- a difference (~0.003) far outside `pytest.approx`'s default relative tolerance, so the existing `position['protective_stop'] == pytest.approx(_QUIET_STOP)` assertion alone now discriminates without needing a new assertion. Verified end-to-end by reverting `app/api/routers/portfolio.py::get_risk`'s `drop_malformed_daily_bars` call locally (`daily_ohlcv = e.daily_ohlcv`): this test now fails with exactly that computed value (`98.4624584717608 == 98.46530612244898 ± 9.8e-05` -> assertion error), then restored the fix and confirmed all 488 backend tests pass again (99.84% coverage, unchanged).
decisions.alternatives_considered: Inserting at index 1 was also confirmed by hand-computation to discriminate (98.45049833887043 vs. the reference) and would have worked equally well -- index 2 was picked arbitrarily between the two working options, no material difference. Insertion at index 3, 4, or 5 was tried and rejected: hand-computation showed those positions are, for this specific 6-row fixture and 10-day window, structural no-ops just like index 0 (each reproduces the exact reference stop of 98.46530612244898 whether or not the row is dropped) -- likely because `protective_stop` is called on `daily_ohlcv.iloc[:-1]` in the router (excluding the final 'today' row) and EMA(13)'s exponential decay makes a malformed row close enough to the trailing edge of that already-short window negligible at this tolerance; rather than chase down the exact reason those specific positions happen to cancel out, the two positions (1 and 2) empirically confirmed to perturb the result were preferred. A larger fixture redesign (e.g. a longer clean history so more mid-window positions clearly perturb the result, or a second explicit assertion computing the undropped-frame's protective_stop by hand as a comment) was considered and rejected as unnecessary scope creep -- the existing fixture and existing assertion already discriminate correctly once the insertion point is right, per CLAUDE.md's normal preference for the smallest change that resolves the actual gap.
